learn.hook: Can your hands lie to you? Try this and see: the same water can feel warm to one hand and cool to the other!
points: We often say things are hot, warm, cool or cold. Temperature tells us exactly how hot or cold something is.
Our sense of touch is not reliable for judging temperature.

Try this (with an adult): keep one hand in cool tap water and the other in comfortably warm (not hot) water for a minute. Then put both in normal tap water. The 'cool' hand feels it as warm, and the 'warm' hand feels it as cool!
Never test very hot water, a hot iron or a stove with your hand; it can burn you.
To know temperature correctly and safely, we use a thermometer.

example.q: Two friends dip their hands into the same bucket of water. Simran says 'warm!' and Aditya says 'cool!'. How is this possible?
steps: Just before, Simran had her hand in cold water and Aditya had his hand in warm water.
Our skin compares the new water with what it felt just before.
So the same water feels different to each of them.
example.answer: Touch depends on what the hand felt before, so it is not reliable. A thermometer gives the true temperature.

learn.reallife: Mothers often check a child's forehead for fever by touch, but a doctor always uses a thermometer to be sure.

quiz.q: What does temperature tell us?

options: The same thing can feel hot or cold depending on what we touched before

quiz.q: Which instrument measures temperature?
quiz.explain: A thermometer measures how hot or cold something is.

quiz.q: Rani keeps one hand in cold water and one in warm water, then dips both in tap water. What does the hand from cold water feel?
options: Exactly the same as the other hand
quiz.explain: Compared with the cold water it was in, the tap water feels warm to that hand.

options: Ask an adult to check with a thermometer
quiz.explain: A thermometer gives a safe, correct reading without risking a burn.

quiz.q: Which of these is the coldest?
quiz.explain: Ice from a freezer has the lowest temperature among these.

quiz.q: A doctor wants to know if Arjun has a fever. What will the doctor use?

quiz.explain: Touch can mislead us, so a doctor uses a thermometer to get the exact temperature.

teach.ask: Gappu dips one foot in a puddle: 'It feels warm! My friend says it feels cold. Who's telling the truth?'
teach.praise: Chirp! Touch can trick us because it compares with what we felt before. A thermometer tells the true temperature!
teach.nudge: Can our touch always be trusted? What should we use instead?

learn.hook: A thermometer is like a truthful friend: it never says 'it feels warm', it tells you the exact number!
points: A clinical thermometer measures body temperature. Its range is usually 35 °C to 42 °C.
The normal temperature of the human body is about 37 °C. A temperature above this may mean a fever.
A laboratory thermometer measures the temperature of other things like water. Its range is usually −10 °C to 110 °C.
Digital thermometers show the reading as numbers on a screen. Older thermometers had mercury, which is poisonous, so digital ones are now preferred.

Good habits: wash the thermometer before and after use; hold it away from the tip; for a lab thermometer, keep the bulb in the liquid without touching the container and read it while it is still in the liquid.

example.q: Why should a clinical thermometer NOT be used to measure the temperature of boiling water?
steps: A clinical thermometer reads only up to about 42 °C.
Boiling water is at about 100 °C, far above that range.
The thermometer could break, and it cannot show the reading.
example.answer: Its range (35 °C to 42 °C) is too small. Use a laboratory thermometer (with an adult) instead.

learn.reallife: During a fever, a digital thermometer under the tongue or in the armpit beeps when the reading is ready. School labs use laboratory thermometers to measure the temperature of water.

quiz.q: What is the normal temperature of the human body, in °C?
quiz.explain: The normal body temperature is about 37 °C.
quiz.mistake: Confuses body temperature with boiling point or room temperature

quiz.q: What is the usual range of a clinical thermometer?
quiz.explain: Body temperature stays within a small range, so a clinical thermometer reads from 35 °C to 42 °C.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the ranges of clinical and laboratory thermometers

quiz.q: Which thermometer would you use to measure the temperature of hot water in a lab?
quiz.explain: A laboratory thermometer has a range of about −10 °C to 110 °C, suitable for hot water.
quiz.mistake: Thinks a clinical thermometer can measure any temperature

quiz.q: Why are digital thermometers preferred over mercury thermometers?
options: Mercury is poisonous if the thermometer breaks
Digital thermometers are made of glass
quiz.explain: Mercury is toxic and harmful if a glass thermometer breaks. Digital ones avoid this.
quiz.mistake: Does not know the danger of mercury

quiz.q: When reading a laboratory thermometer in water, you should:
options: Take it out first, then read it
Let the bulb touch the bottom of the beaker
Read it while the bulb is still in the water
quiz.explain: Once taken out, the reading starts to change. Read it while the bulb is in the water.
quiz.mistake: Takes the thermometer out before reading

quiz.q: Kabir's thermometer shows 39 °C. What does this suggest?
quiz.explain: 39 °C is higher than the normal 37 °C, so he likely has a fever.
quiz.mistake: Does not compare the reading with normal body temperature

quiz.q: Why should you wash a clinical thermometer before and after use?
quiz.explain: Washing removes germs so that infections do not spread.
quiz.mistake: Does not think about hygiene

quiz.q: What is the usual range of a laboratory thermometer?
quiz.explain: A laboratory thermometer reads from about −10 °C to 110 °C.
quiz.mistake: Confuses the laboratory range with the clinical range

teach.ask: Gappu feels hot and sleepy: 'Do I have a fever? Which thermometer should I use, and what is normal?'
teach.praise: Tweet! A clinical or digital thermometer checks body temperature. About 37 °C is normal; higher may mean fever. I'll rest now!
teach.nudge: Which thermometer is for the body? And what number is normal?

learn.hook: Ice melts at 0 and water boils at 100. That's the clever idea behind the Celsius scale!
points: Temperature is commonly measured in degrees Celsius, written °C.
On the Celsius scale, pure water freezes (and ice melts) at 0 °C and water boils at 100 °C, at normal air pressure.
The scale is named after the Swedish scientist Anders Celsius.
The SI unit of temperature is the kelvin (K), but in daily life we mostly use °C. Some thermometers also show °F; normal body temperature is about 98.6 °F.
Weather reports give the day's maximum (highest) and minimum (lowest) temperatures in °C.

example.q: In Shimla one winter morning it was 4 °C. By afternoon it was 13 °C. By how many degrees did the temperature rise?

learn.reallife: On the evening news you may hear: 'Today's maximum temperature was 41 °C and minimum 28 °C.' That is the Celsius scale at work.

quiz.q: At what temperature does pure water boil at normal air pressure, in °C?
quiz.explain: Water boils at 100 °C at normal air pressure.
quiz.mistake: Confuses the boiling point with the freezing point or body temperature

quiz.q: At what temperature does ice melt, in °C?
quiz.explain: Ice melts, and pure water freezes, at 0 °C.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up melting and boiling points

quiz.q: The Celsius scale is named after:
quiz.explain: Anders Celsius was a Swedish scientist who proposed the scale.
quiz.mistake: Guesses a famous scientist without linking the name

quiz.q: What is the SI unit of temperature?
quiz.explain: The kelvin (K) is the SI unit, though °C is used more in daily life.
quiz.mistake: Thinks °C is the SI unit

quiz.q: A weather report says the maximum temperature was 38 °C and the minimum 26 °C. What is the difference, in °C?
quiz.explain: Difference = 38 − 26 = 12 °C.
quiz.mistake: Adds instead of subtracting

quiz.q: The temperature in a town was 15 °C at 6 am and 24 °C at 2 pm. By how much did it rise, in °C?
quiz.mistake: Adds the two temperatures

2 pm

quiz.q: Normal body temperature is about 37 °C. About what is it in °F?
quiz.explain: 37 °C is the same as about 98.6 °F on the Fahrenheit scale.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the number stays the same on both scales

quiz.q: How many degrees are there between the freezing point and boiling point of water on the Celsius scale?
quiz.explain: From 0 °C to 100 °C is 100 degrees.
quiz.mistake: Confuses Celsius with the Fahrenheit boiling point

teach.ask: Gappu reads a weather report: 'It says 30 degrees Celsius! What is this Celsius scale, and what are its special numbers?'
teach.praise: Chirp chirp! On the Celsius scale, water freezes at 0 °C and boils at 100 °C. 30 °C means a warm day for flying!
teach.nudge: What happens to water at 0 °C, and what happens at 100 °C?
